{{short description|Geometrical plane which second-order contacts a submanifold}}
{{More citations needed|date=January 2023}}
[[Image:frenet.svg|thumb|300px|right|A space curve, [[Frenet–Serret formulas|Frenet–Serret frame]], and the osculating plane ([[Linear span|spanned]] by {{math|'''T'''}} and {{math|'''N'''}}).]]
 
In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[differential geometry]], an '''osculating plane''' is a [[plane (mathematics)|plane]] in a [[Euclidean space]] or [[affine space]] which meets a [[submanifold]] at a [[Point (geometry)|point]] in such a way as to have a second order of [[contact (mathematics)|contact]] at the point.  The word ''osculate'' is {{ety|la|osculari|to kiss}}; an osculating plane is thus a plane which "kisses" a submanifold.

The osculating plane in the geometry of Euclidean space curves can be described in terms of the [[Frenet-Serret formulas]] as the [[linear span]] of the tangent and normal vectors.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Do Carmo |first=Manfredo |author-link=Manfredo do Carmo |title=Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces |isbn=978-0486806990 |edition=2nd |pages=18}}</ref>
